messages:
Raj: Quick RFC follow-up idea: introduce a "ownership_cooloff" window + explicit PREHOLD/CLAIM states for prefix leases. Goal: reduce oscillation when many nodes try to claim hot prefixes. Thoughts?

Nina: I like the idea. Can you expand PREHOLD vs CLAIM semantics?

Raj: PREHOLD is a soft intent written by candidate owner (no immediate demote). CLAIM is the atomic takeover that increments epoch. During cooloff_ms after CLAIM we reject reclaim attempts. PREHOLD allows the system to plan rebalances without thrashing.

Tom: How do clients see this? If backend rejects, what error shape? We should avoid generic 5xxs. Propose: PREFIX_PREHOLD_HINT (soft) and PREFIX_EPOCH_CLAIMED (hard) with metadata {epoch, backoff_ms}.

Jules: If we return epoch info, router can re-route without full discovery. Also we should make prefetch cancellations explicit: prefetch tasks carry expected_epoch and drop silently if mismatch.

Raj: Example state transitions (sketch):

```
PREHOLD -> (after prep) -> CLAIM -> OWNED
OWNED -> (demote requested) -> PREPARE_DEMOTE -> RELEASE
```

Raj: Config sample: 
```
cooloff_ms: 3000
prehold_ttl_ms: 500
claim_retries: 3
proxy_window_ms: 200
```

Nina: Proxy window is interesting: old owner can act as short-lived proxy to reduce client-visible errors. But TOM: need to ensure proxies don't cause unbounded load. Add circuit-breaker per-prefix for proxying.

Tom: Agreed. Circuit breaker states: CLOSED (proxy allowed), OPEN (no proxy, return epoch error), HALF_OPEN (probe). Default threshold: 200 reqs/s or 50ms latency increase.

Jules: About correctness: garbage collection and tombstone compaction must respect epochs. Compactor only cleans entries with tombstone_epoch < current_min_epoch_per_prefix. Otherwise we risk data loss.

Raj: Good catch. We'll track min_active_epoch per node and expose it to compactor service. Also add a tiny audit log for last 10 handoffs for debugging.

ops-bot: Metric suggestions logged: prefix.proxy.circuit_open_total, prefix.claim.attempts, prefix.cooloff.rejects. See https://internal/metrics/prefix-handoff

Nina: Testing plan: small chaos job that blips nodes and forces repeated preholds/claims, measure mismatch rate and p99 client latency. Also simulate RPC delays to validate proxy circuit.

Tom: Implementation note: use CAS on lease record. Do not hold global locks. Make claim fast path: single CAS and publish event to watchers.

Raj: I'll prototype claim state machine + proxy circuit and run the chaos tests this week. Will post results and a short PR with API error shapes.

Jules: If prototype looks good we can standardize error codes and add docs for clients on retry strategies.

Raj: Thanks all. Marking this thread as the coordination anchor for the spike.
